newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - June 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - June 18.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Wednesday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* Lucent Technologies Inc and Philips Electronics NV have agreed to merge their consumer communications products businesses into a jointly owned company.
* Initial construction of new homes and apartments dropped 4.8 percent in May.

* Gateway 2000 Inc said it expects revenues for the second quarter to be about flat with the first quarter. Another computer company, Seagate Technology Inc, said results would be worse than in its prior prediction.
* The number of delinquent credit-card accounts fell in the first quarter.
* Fidelity Investments is expected to announce a round of layoffs that would affect between 280 and 300 people.
* Two French ministers raised further doubts about Europe's plans for a common currency, but French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin reaffirmed his nation's support for the euro.

* R.J. Reynolds sued the Federal Trade Commission, contending it engaged in politically motivated "harassment" and did not follow proper procedures in its efforts to ban the Joe Camel cartoon character.
* Packard Bell NEC plans to sell personal computers directy to business customers.
* Louis Navellier's successful fight against a mutual fund's trustees has led other fund executives to consider what role independent trustees should play in the business.
* Three exercise-equipment makers and an infomercial producer have agreed to settle allegations by the Federal Trade Commission that it could not support some claims made in the ads.
* Japan's trade surplus surged more than 200 percent in May, stirring concerns about the growing trade imbalance with other countries.
* Royal Caribbean Cruises Ltd has agreed to acquire Celebrity Cruise Lines Inc for about $1.3 billion in cash, stock and assumed debt, giving rival Carnival Cruises a run for its money.
* AMR Corp's American Eagle has ordered 67 aircraft from Bombardier of Canada and Embraer of Brazil worth about $1.4 billion.
* Lockheed Martin Corp has ordered 101 rocket engines to be built jointly by Russian firm NPO Energomash and United Technologies Corp's Pratt & Whitney.
* The Dow Jones Industrials dropped 11.31 points, closing at 7760.78.
* Heard on the Street: The jokes, mostly tasteless, used to fly free and easy on Wall Street. These days, though, the humor mill has hit a bear market.
* Credit Markets: A broad range of institutional investors have signed up to buy $400 million of bonds whose performance hinges on the severity of hurricanes striking the United States.
